Event.flag.refreshed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It reports that the feature-flag payload was re-fetched and carries only a source label and a count, not the flags themselves. No replacement — flag values are resolved per call. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.project.updated.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. Read project state with the `project.current` / `project.list` SDK methods instead; the fields that actually change during a session (the VCS branch) have their own event, `vcs.branch.updated`. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.config.managed.policy_changed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It was added for a managed-config consent dialog that was never built, so today the policy change is applied and the event is dropped. No replacement — read the managed config directly if you need to detect a policy change. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

header.description: Very short label shown as a tab/chip (about 12 chars; longer is truncated). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: Available choices (2-4, distinct; do NOT include an 'Other' option — it is added automatically)

multiple.description: Allow selecting multiple choices (phrase the question accordingly)

Event.memory.extraction.completed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It is memory-v2 telemetry, not a supported integration point — counts and timings are also written to the `memory` service log. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.memory.consolidation.completed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It is memory-v2 telemetry, not a supported integration point — counts and timings are also written to the `memory` service log. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.memory.recall.completed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It is memory-v2 telemetry, not a supported integration point — counts and timings are also written to the `memory` service log. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.mcp.tools.changed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It fires on an MCP `notifications/tools/list_changed` and on config reload, and only carries a server name — the cache is already invalidated by the time it is published, so re-reading the tool list is enough. Note `mcp.status.changed` is NOT a drop-in replacement: it tracks connection state, not tool-list changes. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.schedule.created.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event, and there is no HTTP route or SDK method behind it — schedules are managed only through the `schedule` tool. A fired schedule surfaces as an ordinary session (`session.created`, then `session.idle` when it finishes). Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

directory.description: project directory this task runs in

Event.schedule.updated.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event, and there is no HTTP route or SDK method behind it — schedules are managed only through the `schedule` tool. A fired schedule surfaces as an ordinary session (`session.created`, then `session.idle` when it finishes). Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

directory.description: project directory this task runs in

Event.schedule.removed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event, and there is no HTTP route or SDK method behind it — schedules are managed only through the `schedule` tool. A fired schedule surfaces as an ordinary session (`session.created`, then `session.idle` when it finishes). Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.schedule.fired.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event, and there is no HTTP route or SDK method behind it — schedules are managed only through the `schedule` tool. A fired schedule surfaces as an ordinary session (`session.created`, then `session.idle` when it finishes). Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

activeForm.description: Present-continuous form of the task for display while in_progress (e.g. 'Running tests' for 'Run tests'). Optional — only needed when a natural present-continuous phrasing differs meaningfully from content.

status.description: Current status of the task: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled

priority.description: Priority level of the task: high, medium, low

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item

blocks.description: ids of tasks this task blocks (they wait on this one)

blocked_by.description: ids of tasks that must complete before this one can start

Event.agent.thread.created.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. A created thread is observable through the child session it drives (`session.created`) and through `agent.thread.completed` / `agent.thread.error` when it finishes. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.thread.interrupted.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. Interruption is already reported by `session.status` on the interrupted session. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.limit.reached.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. The spawn that hit the limit fails with an error the caller already sees. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.task.activated.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It only signals which running task the tool call is currently attached to, carries nothing but an id, and is not published alongside a `task.updated`, so it cannot be reconstructed from the task list. No replacement — it is going away. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.task.backgrounded.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. `sendToBackground` writes the task first, so the same transition already arrives as a `task.updated` with `isBackground: true` — watch that instead. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.task.deactivated.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It only signals which running task the tool call is currently attached to, carries nothing but an id, and is not published alongside a `task.updated`, so it cannot be reconstructed from the task list. No replacement — it is going away. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

subject.description: A brief title for the work item

activeForm.description: Present-continuous form shown while in_progress (e.g. 'Running tests')

owner.description: Session id of the agent that claimed this item

blocks.description: ids of items this item blocks (they wait on this one)

blocked_by.description: ids of items that must complete before this one can start

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata attached to the item

Event.agent.coordinator.enabled.description: Deprecated: coordinator-internal telemetry with no consumer. Track dispatched work through the child sessions themselves (`session.created`, `session.status`, `session.idle`) or the `task.*` events. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.coordinator.disabled.description: Deprecated: coordinator-internal telemetry with no consumer. Track dispatched work through the child sessions themselves (`session.created`, `session.status`, `session.idle`) or the `task.*` events. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.coordinator.dispatched.description: Deprecated: coordinator-internal telemetry with no consumer. Track dispatched work through the child sessions themselves (`session.created`, `session.status`, `session.idle`) or the `task.*` events. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.coordinator.dispatch_updated.description: Deprecated: coordinator-internal telemetry with no consumer. Track dispatched work through the child sessions themselves (`session.created`, `session.status`, `session.idle`) or the `task.*` events. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.session.notification.queued.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. The notification queue is an internal hand-off — a queued notification reaches the user as part of the next assistant turn, observable through `message.part.updated`. No direct replacement. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.session.notification.drained.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. The notification queue is an internal hand-off — a queued notification reaches the user as part of the next assistant turn, observable through `message.part.updated`. No direct replacement. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.session.tool_summary.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It carries a short progress label for a batch of tool calls, and it was always intended for clients rather than the TUI — but nothing has ever consumed it. The same information is derivable from the `message.part.updated` tool parts. Scheduled for removal in the next major unless a consumer is written first; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.team.created.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. Team membership is state, not a stream — read it back through the `team` tool. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.agent.team.deleted.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. Team membership is state, not a stream — read it back through the `team` tool. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.pty.created.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event — the PTY WebSocket at `GET /pty/{ptyID}/connect` reports session lifecycle to the only client that has ever used it. Poll `GET /pty` for the session list. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.pty.updated.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event — the PTY WebSocket at `GET /pty/{ptyID}/connect` reports session lifecycle to the only client that has ever used it. Poll `GET /pty` for the session list. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.pty.exited.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event — the PTY WebSocket at `GET /pty/{ptyID}/connect` reports session lifecycle to the only client that has ever used it. Poll `GET /pty` for the session list. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.pty.deleted.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event — the PTY WebSocket at `GET /pty/{ptyID}/connect` reports session lifecycle to the only client that has ever used it. Poll `GET /pty` for the session list. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

Event.global.disposed.description: Deprecated: no consumer reads this event. It is emitted once on `POST /global/dispose`, which itself has no caller in this repo, and it carries no payload. Per-instance disposal is reported by `server.instance.disposed`, which is consumed and is not going away. Scheduled for removal in the next major; still emitted until then.

KeybindsConfig.description: Remap keyboard shortcuts. Every action listed here has a default; only the ones you set are overridden. Use <leader> to build on the leader key, separate alternatives with commas to bind several chords to one action, and set "none" to leave an action unbound.

leader.description: Prefix key that opens a two-key chord. Press it, then the second key within 2 seconds; every `<leader>…` binding below is built on it.

app_exit.description: Quit 100xprompt. In the prompt it only quits when the input is empty — with text typed, ctrl+c hits `input_clear` first and just clears it. Inside a dialog or a permission prompt this key cancels instead of quitting.

editor_open.description: Open the current prompt in $EDITOR. Whatever you save comes back into the prompt, and @file/@agent mentions are re-anchored to wherever their text ended up.

scrollbar_toggle.description: Show or hide the scrollbar alongside the session transcript.

task_background.description: Accepted for compatibility but currently inert — nothing in the TUI reads this binding. Background tasks are reached from the command palette ("Background tasks").

username_toggle.description: Accepted for compatibility but currently inert — this build has no username display to toggle and nothing reads this binding.

status_view.description: Open the status panel: version, providers, connected MCP servers and the active directories.

session_export.description: Export the transcript as Markdown. Asks what to include, writes the file into the current directory and opens it in $EDITOR; edits you make there are saved back to the file.

session_new.description: Start a new session, carrying anything already typed in the prompt across to it.

session_timeline.description: Open the message timeline and jump to any earlier point in the session.

session_fork.description: Pick an earlier message and branch a new session from it, leaving this one intact.

session_share.description: Publish a share link for this session and copy it to the clipboard. Hidden when `share` is set to "disabled".

session_interrupt.description: Abort the turn in flight. Only active while the session is busy; in shell (!) mode it leaves shell mode instead.

session_compact.description: Summarize the session so far and carry on from the summary, reclaiming context. Needs a provider connected.

messages_page_up.description: Scroll the transcript up by half a viewport. (The name is inherited; the step really is half a screen, and `messages_half_page_up` is a quarter.)

messages_page_down.description: Scroll the transcript down by half a viewport. (The name is inherited; the step really is half a screen, and `messages_half_page_down` is a quarter.)

messages_half_page_up.description: Scroll the transcript up by a quarter of a viewport — half the step `messages_page_up` takes.

messages_half_page_down.description: Scroll the transcript down by a quarter of a viewport — half the step `messages_page_down` takes.

messages_first.description: Jump to the top of the transcript.

messages_last.description: Jump to the bottom of the transcript.

messages_next.description: Scroll to the next message boundary.

messages_previous.description: Scroll to the previous message boundary.

messages_last_user.description: Jump to the most recent message you actually typed, skipping synthetic and hidden text.

messages_copy.description: Copy the last assistant message to the clipboard, also emitting OSC 52 so it works over SSH and inside tmux.

messages_undo.description: Roll the session back to before your previous message and restore that message's text and attachments into the prompt. Aborts the turn in flight first.

messages_redo.description: Step forward again after an undo, restoring the next message. Only available while a message is reverted.

messages_toggle_conceal.description: Collapse or expand fenced code blocks in the transcript. Shares its default with `tips_toggle`, which is only live on the home screen, so the two never collide.

feedback_up.description: Rate the last Auto-routed response as good (👍). Does nothing if the last response was not Auto-routed.

feedback_down.description: Rate the last Auto-routed response as bad (👎). Does nothing if the last response was not Auto-routed.

tool_details.description: Show or hide the expanded output underneath each tool call.

model_cycle_recent.description: Switch to the next model in your recently-used list without opening the picker.

model_cycle_recent_reverse.description: Switch to the previous model in your recently-used list without opening the picker.

model_cycle_favorite.description: Switch to the next favourited model. Warns if you have not starred any.

model_cycle_favorite_reverse.description: Switch to the previous favourited model. Warns if you have not starred any.

command_list.description: Open the command palette — every action in one searchable list.

permission_mode_cycle.description: Cycle the session's permission mode: default → acceptEdits → auto → plan → back to default.

variant_cycle.description: Cycle the model's thinking / reasoning-effort level: model default → each level the model offers → back to default. Does nothing on models with no levels.

input_clear.description: Clear the prompt. Only fires while there is text; on an empty prompt the same default falls through to `app_exit`.

input_paste.description: Paste the system clipboard into the prompt. An image on the clipboard is attached as a file part instead of pasted as text.

input_newline.description: Insert a line break without sending.

input_move_left.description: Move the cursor one character left.

input_move_right.description: Move the cursor one character right.

input_move_up.description: Move the cursor up one wrapped row.

input_move_down.description: Move the cursor down one wrapped row.

input_select_left.description: Inert. The prompt editor has no selection model, and unlike the other `input_select_*` keys this one is not wired to a cursor move either.

input_select_right.description: Inert. The prompt editor has no selection model, and unlike the other `input_select_*` keys this one is not wired to a cursor move either.

input_select_up.description: Moves the cursor up one wrapped row. The prompt editor has no selection model, so nothing is highlighted.

input_select_down.description: Moves the cursor down one wrapped row. The prompt editor has no selection model, so nothing is highlighted.

input_line_home.description: Move the cursor to the start of the current line.

input_line_end.description: Move the cursor to the end of the current line.

input_select_line_home.description: Moves the cursor to the start of the line — identical to `input_line_home`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_select_line_end.description: Moves the cursor to the end of the line — identical to `input_line_end`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_visual_line_home.description: Move the cursor to the start of the current line. Identical to `input_line_home` today: this movement works on real lines, not wrapped rows.

input_visual_line_end.description: Move the cursor to the end of the current line. Identical to `input_line_end` today: this movement works on real lines, not wrapped rows.

input_select_visual_line_home.description: Moves the cursor to the start of the line — identical to `input_line_home`. No selection model, and no wrapped-row behaviour either.

input_select_visual_line_end.description: Moves the cursor to the end of the line — identical to `input_line_end`. No selection model, and no wrapped-row behaviour either.

input_buffer_home.description: Move the cursor to the very start of the prompt.

input_buffer_end.description: Move the cursor to the very end of the prompt.

input_select_buffer_home.description: Moves the cursor to the very start of the prompt — identical to `input_buffer_home`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_select_buffer_end.description: Moves the cursor to the very end of the prompt — identical to `input_buffer_end`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_delete_line.description: Delete from the cursor to the end of the line — the same edit as `input_delete_to_line_end`, despite the name. The whole line is not removed.

input_delete_to_line_end.description: Delete from the cursor to the end of the line.

input_delete_to_line_start.description: Delete from the start of the line up to the cursor.

input_backspace.description: Delete the character before the cursor.

input_delete.description: Delete the character after the cursor.

input_undo.description: Undo the last edit to the prompt text. This is the prompt's own edit history — to undo a sent message use `messages_undo`.

input_redo.description: Redo an edit to the prompt text undone by `input_undo`.

input_word_forward.description: Move the cursor one word right.

input_word_backward.description: Move the cursor one word left.

input_select_word_forward.description: Moves the cursor one word right — identical to `input_word_forward`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_select_word_backward.description: Moves the cursor one word left — identical to `input_word_backward`. The prompt editor has no selection model.

input_delete_word_forward.description: Delete from the cursor forward to the end of the word.

input_delete_word_backward.description: Delete from the cursor back to the start of the word.

history_previous.description: Recall the previous prompt you submitted. Only fires when the cursor is already at the very start of the prompt, so it never fights with cursor movement.

history_next.description: Recall the next prompt in history. Only fires when the cursor is already at the very end of the prompt, so it never fights with cursor movement.

session_child_cycle.description: Move to the next sub-session spawned by this one.

session_child_cycle_reverse.description: Move to the previous sub-session spawned by this one.

session_parent.description: Go back up to the session that spawned this one.

terminal_suspend.description: Suspend to the shell (SIGTSTP). Bring it back with `fg` and the UI redraws.

terminal_title_toggle.description: Turn terminal window-title updates on or off. The choice is remembered between runs.

tips_toggle.description: Show or hide the tips block on the home screen. Only bound on the home screen — inside a session the same default runs `messages_toggle_conceal`.

sprites_toggle.description: Show or hide the companion sprite in the session view. The choice is remembered between runs.

LogLevel.description: Lowest severity written to the log file. DEBUG is the most detailed and ERROR the least.

ServerConfig.description: Where the HTTP server binds and who may talk to it. Applies to `100xprompt serve` and anything else that starts the server.

port.description: Port the HTTP server binds to. Leave unset to try 4096 first and fall back to any free port. `--port` on the command line wins over this.

hostname.description: Address the HTTP server binds to. Defaults to 127.0.0.1, or 0.0.0.0 when `mdns` is on and no hostname is set here. `--hostname` on the command line wins over this.

mdns.description: Advertise the server over mDNS/Bonjour so other machines on the LAN can find it. Skipped with a warning if the server is bound to loopback, since nothing off-box could reach it anyway.

cors.description: Extra origins allowed to call the HTTP server, matched exactly. localhost, 127.0.0.1, tauri://localhost and *.100xprompt.com/.ai are already allowed. Any `--cors` values are added to this list rather than replacing it.

PermissionConfig.description: What may run without asking. Each tool maps to allow (run silently), ask (prompt first) or deny (refuse outright); bash and edit can also take per-pattern rules so, say, `git status` is allowed while `git push` still prompts.

additionalDirectories.description: Extra directories agents may operate in beyond the workspace root. Org policy can pin these as an immutable directory boundary.

workspaceRoot.description: Policy-pinned workspace root. Highest-precedence directory boundary; overrides the env var.

tools.description: Superseded by `permission`. Kept working by translation: true becomes an allow rule and false a deny rule for that tool name, with write/edit/patch/multiedit all collapsing onto the single `edit` permission. Anything set in `permission` overrides the result, so prefer that.

description.description: Description of when to use the agent

hidden.description: Hide this subagent from the @ autocomplete menu (default: false, only applies to mode: subagent)

slim.description: Use a slim system prompt when this agent runs as a spawned subagent: skips memory, mode prompts, and the full environment block (default: true for task-spawned subagents; set false to opt out)

color.description: Hex color code for the agent (e.g., #FF5733)

steps.description: Maximum number of agentic iterations before forcing text-only response

disabled.description: Disable this variant for the model

enterpriseUrl.description: GitHub Enterprise URL for copilot authentication

setCacheKey.description: Enable promptCacheKey for this provider (default false)

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for requests to this provider. Default is 300000 (5 minutes). Set to false to disable timeout.

anyOf.description: Timeout in milliseconds for requests to this provider. Default is 300000 (5 minutes). Set to false to disable timeout.
Disable timeout for this provider entirely.

command.description: Command and arguments to run the MCP server

environment.description: Environment variables to set when running the MCP server

enabled.description: Enable or disable the MCP server on startup

timeout.description: Timeout in ms for fetching tools from the MCP server. Defaults to 5000 (5 seconds) if not specified.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID. If not provided, dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) will be attempted.

clientSecret.description: OAuth client secret (if required by the authorization server)

scope.description: OAuth scopes to request during authorization

url.description: URL of the remote MCP server

enabled.description: Enable or disable the MCP server on startup

headers.description: Headers to send with the request

oauth.description: OAuth authentication configuration for the MCP server. Set to false to disable OAuth auto-detection.

timeout.description: Timeout in ms for fetching tools from the MCP server. Defaults to 5000 (5 seconds) if not specified.

LayoutConfig.description: No longer has any effect. The terminal UI sizes itself to the window and has no alternative layouts; the key is still accepted so older config files keep validating.

PermissionModeConfig.description: Permission mode new sessions start in. --permission-mode and mid-session toggles still override it.

PermissionsConfig.description: Claude Code-style structured permissions: allow/deny/ask rule strings plus defaultMode and disableBypassPermissionsMode. Merged with `permission` (structured rules take precedence). See https://100xprompt.com/docs/permissions

deny.description: CC-style deny rules — deny always wins over allow for a tool

ask.description: CC-style ask rules — force a prompt even when another rule allows

disableBypassPermissionsMode.description: When "disable", removes bypassPermissions from the settable modes for this project.

$schema.description: URL of the schema this file is validated against. Set it to https://proxy.100xprompt.com/config.json to get completion and inline documentation in your editor.

theme.description: Colour theme for the terminal UI. Accepts any built-in theme name or one defined in a themes/ directory. Omit to follow the terminal's own palette.

sandbox.description: Enable the OS command sandbox (seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux). Default: OFF on macOS, ON elsewhere. Set true to opt in on macOS, false to opt out anywhere.

sandboxAutoApprove.description: Skip the bash permission prompt for commands the sandbox actually contains, since the kernel is already enforcing the boundary. Default: ON wherever the sandbox is active. Commands that can exfiltrate data (curl, ssh, rsync…), dangerous commands, and denied/plan-mode commands always still prompt. Set false to always prompt.

sandboxBackend.description: Which sandbox backend confines untrusted bash commands. Default: seatbelt on macOS, landlock on Linux (unset = platform default, unchanged behavior). "microvm" runs each command in a VM-isolated environment with its own kernel — detected via HUNDREDXPROMPT_MICROVM_RUNNER or a `msb` (microsandbox), `docker`, `podman`, or apple `container` CLI on PATH (image: HUNDREDXPROMPT_MICROVM_IMAGE, default alpine). If no runner is present it degrades gracefully to the platform sandbox. "seatbelt"/"landlock" pin that backend (honored only on the matching OS); "none" disables the sandbox like sandbox: false.

tui.description: Behaviour of the terminal UI itself — scrolling feel and how diffs are laid out.

scroll_speed.description: Rows moved per mouse-wheel notch in the transcript. Default 3. Ignored when `scroll_acceleration.enabled` is true, which replaces the fixed step entirely.

scroll_acceleration.description: Momentum scrolling for the transcript, in place of a fixed rows-per-notch step. Overrides `scroll_speed` when enabled.

enabled.description: Turn on the acceleration curve. Flick the wheel and the transcript keeps travelling; a slow scroll stays precise.

diff_style.description: How file diffs are laid out. "auto" (the default) shows them side by side once the terminal is wider than 120 columns and stacks them below that; "stacked" always keeps the single-column unified view.

command.description: Custom slash commands, keyed by the name you type after '/'. See https://100xprompt.com/docs/commands

watcher.description: Which paths the file watcher pays attention to while a session is open.

ignore.description: Extra glob patterns to ignore, on top of .gitignore and the built-in exclusions.

plugin.description: Plugins to load, each either an npm package (optionally @version, defaulting to latest) or a file:// path to a local module. Loaded in addition to the built-in plugins.

hooks.description: Lifecycle hooks (command, prompt, agent, http) keyed by event: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, PermissionRequest, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, PreCompact, PostCompact, and more

matcher.description: Regex matched against the tool name (PreToolUse/PostToolUse only)

command.description: Shell command. Receives the event JSON on stdin

model.description: Model as provider/model (defaults to the small model)

verification.description: Adversarial verification gate — require a read-only verifier subagent verdict before completion reporting on significant changes

enabled.description: Enable the adversarial verification gate: significant turns (threshold+ files modified) cannot mark the final todo completed until a verification subagent has issued VERDICT: PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL. Default false

threshold.description: Distinct files modified in a turn before verification is required. Default 3

agent.description: Subagent spawned to verify the work (default: verifier)

kairos.description: Kairos mode — Claude Code-style background pacing (tick loop + model-controlled sleep) with terminal-focus-aware autonomy

enabled.description: Enable the /kairos TUI command: a background tick loop where the model paces itself with the sleep tool and calibrates autonomy to terminal focus. Default true; set false to disable

default_sleep.description: Seconds to wait before the next tick when the model didn't call sleep. Default 60

vim.description: Enable Vim keybindings in the TUI prompt input

recap.description: Show an end-of-turn recap (Crunched for … + a one-line summary of what changed). Default on.

output_style.description: Active output style (built-in: explanatory, learning, concise; or a custom output-styles/*.md name)

tool_search.description: Defer MCP tool schemas behind a `tool_search` tool to save context. Deferred by default when more than 8 MCP tools are available; set false to disable, true to always defer, or a number to use a custom threshold

snapshot.description: Whether to record a restorable snapshot of the working tree before edits, which is what makes reverting a turn possible. On by default; set false to skip it entirely.

share.description: Who can be given a link to a session. 'manual' (the default) shares only when you ask for it; 'auto' publishes every new session as it starts; 'disabled' refuses to share at all and hides the share command.

autoshare.description: Superseded by `share`. Setting this to true is rewritten to `share: "auto"` when the config loads, and only when `share` is not set — so if you set both, `share` wins. Nothing else reads this key.

autoupdate.description: What to do when a newer release exists: true installs it in the background, 'notify' only mentions it and leaves the upgrade to you, false stops checking altogether.

disabled_providers.description: Provider ids to leave out even though credentials for them were found. Use this to stop a provider you have keys for from being offered.

enabled_providers.description: Provider ids to allow, as an exclusive list: once this is set, every provider not named here is ignored regardless of available credentials.

model.description: The model each new session starts on, written as provider/model — for example anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 or 100xprompt/pro. Leave unset to use the best model your credentials allow.

fallback_model.description: Model to retry with, as provider/model, when the primary one is rate-limited, overloaded, or otherwise refusing work. Pick something on a different provider so a single outage cannot take out both.

small_model.description: Cheaper model, as provider/model, for the small side-jobs that run alongside a conversation: session titles, summaries and similar. Never used for your actual turns.

advisor_model.description: Stronger model consulted by the /second-opinion command, in the format of provider/model. Defaults to the strongest available model

plan_model.description: Stronger model to use when the session is in plan mode (e.g. 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-5'). When set and the session permission mode is 'plan', requests use this model instead of the session's normal model. Supports provider/model format or a short alias (e.g. 'opus').

enabled.description: Master switch for the memory system: extraction, consolidation, recall, and context injection. Default true

extraction.description: Turn-end automatic memory extraction via the side-model. Default true

consolidation.description: Periodic automatic memory consolidation (auto-dream) job. Default true

recall.description: Per-message query-relevant memory recall via the side-model. Default true

model.description: Override the side-model used for memory extraction/consolidation/recall, in the format of provider/model

team.description: Shared / team memory backend (Firestore). When a workspace id and GCP credentials are configured, memory is shared across the team with per-record access control; otherwise memory stays local-only.

workspace.description: Team/workspace id. When set (together with GCP credentials) team memory is enabled: memories can be shared with the workspace and are stored in Firestore under this namespace. Off by default.

user.description: Stable id for the current user within the workspace, used as the memory owner and to filter private memories. Defaults to the OS username when omitted.

project_id.description: GCP project id for Firestore. Falls back to the GCP_PROJECT_ID / GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variables when omitted.

credentials.description: Path to a GCP service-account JSON key file for Firestore, or the JSON itself. Falls back to Application Default Credentials (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS) when omitted.

collection.description: Root Firestore collection for team memories (default 'team-memories').

default_visibility.description: Visibility applied to new memories written while team mode is on (default 'private'). Reads always merge the user's private memories with team-visible ones.

default_agent.description: Default agent to use when none is specified. Must be a primary agent. Falls back to 'build' if not set or if the specified agent is invalid.

username.description: Name shown against your messages in the transcript. Defaults to your operating-system username.

mode.description: Superseded by `agent`. Each entry here is merged into `agent` as a primary agent when the config loads, so existing files keep working — but new configuration belongs under `agent`, which is the only place subagents can be defined.

agent.description: Define or adjust agents, keyed by agent name. The built-ins (build, plan, general, explore and the specialised title/summary/compaction ones) can be reconfigured here, and any other name creates a new agent. See https://100xprompt.com/docs/agent

provider.description: Add providers or change ones already known, keyed by provider id. Use it to point at a self-hosted or OpenAI-compatible endpoint, supply base URLs and headers, or correct the cost and context limits of an individual model.

mcp.description: MCP servers to connect to, keyed by the name their tools are prefixed with. An entry is either a full server definition (a local command to spawn, or a remote URL) or just `{ "enabled": false }` to switch off one declared elsewhere.

enableAllProjectMcpServers.description: Automatically approve every MCP server declared in the project's committed .mcp.json. Security: leave off so untrusted repo servers require explicit opt-in.

enabledMcpjsonServers.description: Names of project .mcp.json MCP servers approved to connect (Claude Code parity)

disabledMcpjsonServers.description: Names of project .mcp.json MCP servers rejected — they never connect (Claude Code parity)

formatter.description: Code formatters run after a file is edited, keyed by formatter name. Override the command or file extensions of a built-in, add your own, disable one with `disabled: true`, or set this whole field to false to format nothing.

lsp.description: Language servers used for diagnostics and symbol lookup, keyed by server id. Override a built-in's command, add a server of your own (`extensions` is required for those), disable one with `disabled: true`, or set this whole field to false to run no language servers.

instructions.description: Extra files whose contents are prepended to the system prompt, as paths or glob patterns relative to the project root. These are read in addition to the AGENTS.md files found automatically, not instead of them.

tools.description: Superseded by `permission`. Kept working by translation: true becomes an allow rule and false a deny rule for that tool name, with write/edit/patch/multiedit all collapsing onto the single `edit` permission. Anything set in `permission` overrides the result, so prefer that.

url.description: Base URL of your organisation's 100xprompt deployment, used to fetch managed configuration.

ttl.description: Prompt-cache lifetime for Anthropic-family models. "1h" (default) keeps the cached prefix alive across long pauses — writes cost 2x base but the prefix is reused instead of re-written every turn, a net win for long interactive/agentic sessions. "5m" writes cheapest (1.25x base input). No effect on non-Anthropic providers.

channel.description: Out-of-band permission approval. Requires HUNDREDXPROMPT_CHANNEL_RELAY=1 and the HMAC key in HUNDREDXPROMPT_CHANNEL_SECRET. There is deliberately no `secret` field here: this file is project-committed, and a committed approval key is a backdoor.

allow.description: Responder identities (chat/user ids) permitted to approve or deny a relayed permission prompt. Empty authorizes nobody.

timeoutMs.description: Approval deadline in ms; on expiry the relay denies. Default 600000.

unreachable.description: 'deny' (default) fails closed when no channel accepted the prompt; 'degrade' falls back to the local dialog. Neither can produce an allow.

chatMaxRetries.description: Number of retries for chat completions on failure

skillEvolve.description: Self-evolving skills (offline, validation-gated). Disabled by default.

enabled.description: Automatically run validation-gated skill evolution on a daily throttle. Default FALSE (manual only — run `100xprompt skills evolve <name>` yourself). Set true to let 100xprompt self-improve your skills in the background, always behind the validation gate (a skill is only changed if it measurably improves on your recent sessions).

skills.description: Restrict auto-evolution to these skill names. Empty/omitted evolves every discovered skill. Manual `skills evolve <name>` is unaffected by this list.

optimizerModel.description: Model (provider/model) that proposes skill edits. Defaults to a strong cheap teacher.

gateMetric.description: Gate comparison metric. 'hard' (default) = binary failure-mode coverage; 'soft' = partial-credit (sensitive to incremental edits); 'mixed' = weighted blend of both (see mixedWeight).

mixedWeight.description: For gateMetric 'mixed': weight given to soft coverage in [0,1]. Default 0.5.

autonomousLr.description: Autonomous learning-rate: scale the per-pass edit budget up/down from recent gate outcomes instead of a fixed budget. Default false (fixed budget).

slowUpdate.description: Epoch-level slow update: maintain a protected long-horizon guidance section in the skill that step edits can't touch. Default false.

dream.description: Dream rollouts + associative recall (synthetic augmentation for sparse data). Default off.

rollouts.description: Synthesize this many contrastive variations per real replay item when held-out data is thin. >1 enables dream augmentation.

recallK.description: Associative recall: pull the K most task-similar past items into tonight's replay set. >0 enables recall.

promptSuggestion.description: Suggested next prompt after each turn (experimental, side-model). Disabled by default.

enabled.description: After each turn ends, a cheap side-model reads the recent conversation and proposes a suggested next prompt in the TUI input footer (accept to fill the input, ignore to dismiss). Default FALSE — fully inert when off: no model call, no render. Interactive CLI only; never fires for SDK/headless/subagent sessions.

variant.description: Suggestion prompt variant. 'user_intent' (default) predicts what the user would naturally type next; 'stated_intent' currently shares the same prompt.

pluginIsolation.description: Run the plugin host in a supervised child process (the VS Code extension-host model): plugins execute out-of-process over JSON-RPC stdio, so a crashing plugin cannot take the agent down and a hung plugin hook is killed and the child restarted (bounded by a restart budget; on exhaustion plugins degrade to unavailable while the agent keeps running). Default FALSE — the in-process plugin host is used. Plugin-provided tools and auth are not served in isolated mode.

persistentRetry.description: Persistent (unattended) transport retry. Disabled by default — strictly additive, interactive behavior unchanged when off.

enabled.description: Unattended/long-running agentic tasks: keep retrying retryable provider failures (429/529/5xx/network) past the interactive ceiling, with capped backoff + heartbeat waits, until maxWaitMs elapses. Default FALSE — interactive sessions stay bounded (fast-fail to the session retry countdown). Background calls still bail on 529; aborts still cancel instantly.

maxWaitMs.description: Hard cap on TOTAL time spent in persistent transport retries for one request. Default 7200000 (2h). The request always fails once this elapses — persistent retry never loops forever.

maxDelayMs.description: Per-attempt backoff ceiling in persistent mode. Default 60000 (60s). Server-directed Retry-After waits are honored in full (clamped to the remaining maxWaitMs budget).

openTelemetry.description: Enable OpenTelemetry spans for AI SDK calls (using the 'experimental_telemetry' flag)

telemetry.description: Opt in to the privacy-first audit/telemetry sink. Disabled by default; can be force-disabled via DO_NOT_TRACK or HUNDREDXPROMPT_TELEMETRY_DISABLE.

telemetryEndpoint.description: Destination URL for telemetry batches. No default — self-hosted / privacy-sensitive by design.

telemetryHeaders.description: Optional headers (e.g. auth) sent with every telemetry batch.

telemetryMode.description: Telemetry wire format: generic JSON batch ('json') or OTLP-compatible logs ('otlp').

telemetrySampleRate.description: Global telemetry sampling rate (0..1, default 1 = keep all). Multiplies each sink's own sampleRate to form its effective keep-probability.

telemetrySinks.description: Multi-sink telemetry routing. When set (non-empty), fully replaces the single telemetryEndpoint field; each sink samples, segments (general/privileged) and retries through its own disk queue independently. Config-driven only — remote/fetched killswitches are out of scope.

endpoint.description: Destination URL for this sink's batches. No default — self-hosted / privacy-sensitive.

headers.description: Optional headers (e.g. auth) sent with every batch for this sink.

mode.description: Wire format for this sink: generic JSON batch ('json') or OTLP-compatible logs ('otlp').

access.description: 'general' (default) receives the sanitized payload with PII-tagged _PROTO_* fields stripped; 'privileged' receives the full payload including _PROTO_* — point only at a trusted first-party store.

enabled.description: Per-sink killswitch. Default true; set false to skip this sink entirely (no payload built).

sampleRate.description: Per-sink sampling rate (0..1, default 1 = keep all).

primary_tools.description: Tools that should only be available to primary agents.

continue_loop_on_deny.description: Continue the agent loop when a tool call is denied

verificationGate.description: Verification-gated stopping: the agent loop cannot end a turn (stop) until a verifier emits a pass verdict (e.g. `bun run typecheck`). Default false — the loop stops as before.

mcp_timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for model context protocol (MCP) requests

env.description: Environment variables injected into the agent's tool environment (e.g. Bash, hooks). Keys and values are plain strings; tools that spawn subprocesses should merge these into their environment.

includeCoAuthoredBy.description: Whether to append a Co-Authored-By trailer to git commits. Defaults to true. Set to false to suppress the trailer (e.g. for repositories that enforce clean commit footers).

statusline.description: Shell command to execute for custom footer status text. Receives session context as JSON on stdin and its stdout is rendered as trailing text in the TUI footer.

worktree.description: Ergonomics for git worktrees created by the enter_worktree tool

sparsePaths.description: Cone-mode sparse-checkout paths. When non-empty, new worktrees check out only these paths instead of the full tree — cheap to branch from a huge repo. Leave unset for a normal full checkout.

symlinkDirectories.description: Directories (e.g. ['node_modules', '.venv']) to symlink from a new worktree back to the main repo, avoiding a costly reinstall. Skipped when the source is missing or the target already exists.
